title: Wren and the Thorn
premise: Oscar Halloran, a temple scribe bound by her father's debts to the magicless valley of Dunlow, discovers tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies hidden in the temple archives—alongside her own name and the words 'the thorn wakes.' The prophecy foretells that whoever reads it will carry the Thorn, a seed of wild magic that cannot survive inside the valley's dead borders, forcing Oscar to flee the only home she's known before the temple's Inquisitors silence her. Hunted across a kingdom where magic is inherited like property and hoarded by noble bloodlines, Oscar learns the ancient war was never ended, only postponed by the valley itself—a prison built on a stolen inheritance. In the end, Oscar must choose between destroying the Thorn and thus keeping power out of anyone's hands forever, or planting it in the valley's soil to return magic to the dispossessed, knowing either act will cost her everything she loves.
about_author: Orsen Okafor is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial land records in West Africa before turning to fiction about documents that refuse to stay quiet. He writes from a farmhouse outside Accra, where he keeps an unreadable book on his shelf as a reminder that some stories choose their readers.

chapters.title: The Date That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Oscar Halloran, cataloguing the temple's restricted archive to work off her father's debt, finds a prophecy book whose final entry bears tomorrow's date—and her name. Her POV; wonder curdling into dread as she realizes someone wrote this a hundred years ago.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Skin
chapters.summary: Oscar copies the page secretly, but the words transfer onto her own forearm overnight, burning when she lies. POV shifts briefly to Inquisitor Vane, who notices the archive seal broken. Emotional beat: guilt and the first physical sign she cannot undo what she's read.

chapters.title: Debtors' Row
chapters.summary: Oscar visits her father, a broken man paying the family debt in labor at the temple mills, and nearly tells him everything but can't. Her POV; the beat is love constrained by shame, establishing what she stands to lose.

chapters.title: Vane Comes Asking
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vane interrogates the archive staff with polite menace; Oscar lies for the first time in her life and the mark burns so hot she faints. Dual POV (Oscar/Vane); fear becomes concrete as Vane reveals he's been waiting for the prophecy to surface.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgets
chapters.summary: An exiled hedge-witch, Maren, living in the valley's border marshes, recognizes the mark and explains: the valley is a null zone, a cage built a century ago, and the Thorn—a seed of primal magic—now lives in Oscar. Maren's POV framing Oscar's; awe and terror at learning her body is a vessel.

chapters.title: The Gate at Dusk
chapters.summary: Temple guards surround Maren's hut; Oscar flees through the marsh as the valley's border flares behind her, crossing into a world where magic exists for the first time. Oscar's POV; grief and vertigo—the point of no return.

chapters.title: A Kingdom of Inherited Fire
chapters.summary: Outside, Oscar sees magic as visible wealth: noble houses glowing with generational power while peasants are drained by tithe. She meets Tam, a smuggler moving 'unlicensed' magic-touched children to safety. Tam's POV introducing Oscar; righteous anger establishes the theme of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Tithe Wagon
chapters.summary: Oscar joins Tam's crew to rescue children conscripted for blood-harvest by House Corvane; the plan half-succeeds and a child dies. Oscar's POV; the beat is the cost of action—her scribe's hands have blood on them now.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Lord Corvane captures Oscar and offers to buy the Thorn from her blood legally, promising to erase her father's debt; he shows her the original war records proving the valley was built on confiscated commoner magic. Oscar's POV; temptation—justice offered through the very system that corrupted it.

chapters.title: The Mark Speaks
chapters.summary: Imprisoned, Oscar dreams inside the Thorn and meets the echo of its last bearer, who warns that every house that held it rotted from within—including the ones who built the valley to hide it. Dream-sequence POV; horror that the Thorn corrupts even well-meaning bearers.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam trades his smuggling network's secrets to Corvane to free Oscar, betraying his own people; she learns of it after they escape together. Alternating POV; betrayal and the question of whether desperate means ever stay clean.

chapters.title: The Road to Ashfall
chapters.summary: Fugitives now hunted by both Corvane and the temple, Oscar and Tam travel to Ashfall, the ruined pre-war capital where the Thorn was first cut from the world-tree. Oscar's POV; weary intimacy grows between them against a landscape of old atrocities.

chapters.title: Maren Returns
chapters.summary: Maren finds them, revealed as a former Corvane daughter who fled her inheritance; she teaches Oscar to quiet the Thorn rather than use it. Maren's POV; mentorship and the revelation that renouncing power is also a choice with a price.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Second Reader
chapters.summary: Vane catches up, but instead of arresting Oscar he confesses: he read the book years ago and refused the Thorn, and the temple has been hollowing him out ever since as punishment. Vane's POV; pity for the enemy—he is what Oscar becomes if she refuses wrongly.

chapters.title: Ashfall's Library
chapters.summary: In Ashfall's buried archive, Oscar finds the war's true ending: the valley wasn't a refuge, it was a vault where the victors sealed the commons' magic, and the prophecy is the vault's alarm. Oscar's POV; fury—her whole life was a lock's mechanism.

chapters.title: House Against House
chapters.summary: Corvane's rivals learn of the Thorn and march on Ashfall; the noble houses' private war spills into open battle around the ruins. Multiple brief POVs; chaos showing power's corruption metastasizing without needing the Thorn at all.

chapters.title: The Choice in the Vault
chapters.summary: At the valley's heart-mechanism beneath Ashfall, Oscar can destroy the Thorn permanently—killing all magic everywhere—or plant it in the vault soil to return magic to everyone, uninheritable and wild. Oscar's POV alone; the climax of conscience.

chapters.title: Thornwake
chapters.summary: Corvane arrives to take the Thorn by force; in the struggle Oscar is mortally wounded and the Thorn, defending her, erupts—magic flooding back into the world untethered from bloodlines. Climax; terror and terrible beauty as the old order breaks.

chapters.title: What Power Costs
chapters.summary: Dying, Oscar walks into the valley's collapsing border carrying the Thorn's excess, letting the null zone absorb the surge to spare the fleeing crowds; Tam and Maren carry her back through. Tam's POV; sacrifice framed not as martyrdom but as repayment of a debt freely chosen.

chapters.title: The Valley Opens
chapters.summary: The valley's null field dissolves; its people wake to a world where magic belongs to no one and must be learned like any craft. Maren's POV; bittersweet liberation—freedom arriving too late for some, including perhaps Oscar.

chapters.title: The Scribe's Hand
chapters.summary: Oscar survives, scarred and mostly powerless, her debt annulled by a kingdom remaking its laws without inherited magic; she begins writing a new archive—not prophecies, but testimony. Oscar's POV; quiet hope, justice becoming something tended rather than seized.

chapters.title: Wren and the Thorn
chapters.summary: Epilogue: a child finds a new book in the rebuilt archive bearing a future date and a stranger's name; Oscar, now keeper, lets the child decide whether to read. Oscar's POV; the cycle acknowledged but changed—inheritance replaced by invitation.
